headline: HSC and equivalent exam results published today for over 12.70 lakh examinees
summary: The results for more than 1.27 million students will be formally announced at 11:00 AM, with examinees able to check them online and via SMS immediately after.
details: The results of this year's Higher Secondary Certificate (HSC) and equivalent examinations, involving over 12.70 lakh examinees, are being published today.
The formal announcement will take place at 11:00 AM in the meeting room of the Secondary and Higher Education Division, Ministry of Education.

Following the announcement, students can check their results through their educational institutions, designated websites, and SMS. Online access requires roll and registration numbers via eduboardresults.gov.bd and educationboardresults.gov.bd.
Results can also be obtained instantly by sending an SMS to 16140 from any mobile operator, using the prescribed format.

Additionally, applications for re-scrutiny or reassessment of answer scripts will be open from November 1 to November 7. Detailed instructions for this process will be published on the websites of the respective education boards.

Results can also be obtained instantly by sending an SMS to 16140 from any mobile operator, using the prescribed format.

Additionally, applications for re-scrutiny or reassessment of answer scripts will be open from November 1 to November 7. Detailed instructions for this process will be published on the websites of the respective education boards.

headline_marked: [[PBI recovers motorcycle, friend claims Tahsif jumped into Turag]] after chase
headline: PBI recovers motorcycle, friend claims Tahsif jumped into Turag after chase
summary: The Police Bureau of Investigation is probing the death of former airman KM Tahsif Souri. A friend's statement about being chased and Tahsif jumping into the river is being verified, and a motorcycle has been recovered.
details: The Police Bureau of Investigation (PBI) yesterday recovered a motorcycle from Mazar Basti in Tongi, about three kilometres from where former airman KM Tahsif Souri's body was found in the Turag River. This recovery was based on information provided by Tahsif’s friend, Ahmed Shahriar Reza Dip.

Dip told investigators that he and Tahsif were chased by some people in the area on the night Tahsif went missing. He claimed Tahsif jumped into the river while fleeing, but Dip himself managed to escape.

PBI officials are currently cross-checking all information provided by Dip, stating they do not believe everything outright. They are verifying if the recovered black motorcycle is the same one Tahsif was seen riding on CCTV footage before his disappearance.

Initially, Dip mentioned being chased by people in uniform, later specifying two police officers. However, PBI suggested they might have mistaken security guards from a nearby garment factory for police personnel.
Tahsif’s father, AKM Enayetul Karim, dismissed Dip's claim of fleeing from police as
He previously alleged that his son was murdered and his body dumped into the river.

Tahsif, a former Bangladesh Air Force flight lieutenant, left his Uttara home on Tuesday evening and did not return. River police recovered his body from the Turag near Rajabari Ghat in Uttarkhan on Wednesday afternoon.

Tahsif had gained public attention following allegations that he circulated a video clip purportedly showing ousted prime minister Sheikh Hasina leaving the country. PBI took Dip into custody from his Mohammadpur house early yesterday.

A tea stall owner in Mazar Basti reported seeing a motorcycle without a number plate parked there since Wednesday morning, which police later recovered. Investigators are using technological evidence to establish Dip's presence in the area and verify his statements.
PBI is examining the circumstances of why Tahsif and Dip visited the area around 2:00 AM. River Police stated they would file a case if Tahsif’s family does not do so by today.
